reason: Intended difference (RDD finding A): --mask is documented to redact user identities, but Python mask() only masks role-less base64-like runs of 16+ characters, so user names (jdoe, admin, guest, station, root, the 'bad' login attempt) printed in clear. Go applies allowlist masking (rule v4): only framed operation fields and identity-free slot paths print under --mask; everything else in an audit section is masked. A section is an audit section when the schema has an 'operation' field or an AuditRecord record type, or when it holds an AuditEvent operation name anywhere as a plain byte substring. In it a printable run overlapping a framed record's userName (or, for Login/Login Failure/Logout/Logout (Timeout), its slotName, oldValue, value or non-slot-path target) prints <USER-MASKED>; a run prints verbatim only if it equals an AuditEvent operation constant and starts at the first content byte of a framed record's operation field, or starts at the first byte of a framed record's slot-path target, ends inside it, and has no '/'-separated segment equal (ASCII case-insensitive) to an identity-field value of a framed record and no segment after a 'UserService' segment; every other run prints <VALUE-MASKED>, role accounts and operation names outside a framed operation field (here the slotName 'Login' of the Added record) included. stdout below is the corrected expectation; the Python capture in stdout is unchanged.
